I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, that is the system I know best, it fits the local water and weather, and at my age I would rather do steady, familiar work than take price or management risks on crops that need more labor or more delicate timing. Since it is the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage that first, then I will follow it with summer maize on the same land after harvest. I will put all 10 mu into this rotation instead of splitting into many crops, because one simple plan is easier for me to manage, easier to irrigate, and easier to sell.

For the wheat, I will stay with an improved variety instead of saving old seed, because I want stable yield and more even growth. I will fertilize enough to support grain filling but not push it too hard, because too much nitrogen brings lodging and waste. I will irrigate about three times if water is available: once around jointing, once around booting or heading, and once at grain filling if the field is dry. I will spray only when needed, mainly for weeds early and then for disease or aphids if pressure shows up. After wheat harvest, I will seed hybrid summer maize right away. I will use no-tillage for maize after wheat so I do not lose time or moisture. I will give maize most of its fertilizer around planting and the rest at the big bell stage, irrigate around two times depending on rain, and keep pesticide use limited to the main weed and pest periods. This is the plan I would follow because it is practical, familiar, and gives me the best chance of a dependable harvest from the same ground.
